The same face staying toward us is also not uncommon at all. Tidal locking happens fairly frequently. Pluto and Charon are both tidally locked to one another. Stand on one and look at the other, and it won't appear to move in the sky (much, I'm sure there is some wobble). Extrasolar planets around red dwarf stars (by far the most common type) also can get tidally locked, and what makes this problematic for us is that this extends through the habitable zone. Thus, it appears that 90% of the planetary systems out there are incapable of supporting anything resembling a spinning Earth. Any planet close enough to be habitable will also be tidally locked. They may still harbor life, but they won't be particularly hospitable to us. (Fortunately, 10% of the systems still amounts to a LOT.)
